analysis.title: GS Vol Views 28 Oct 2026
key_insights: GS derivatives desk sees AI concerns, Middle East tensions and midterm elections as sources of near-term volatility, while earnings support and lighter positioning (net positioning at 5-year lows per GS PB) could help equities into year-end.

Flows have turned more constructive. Call volumes are about 57% of the tape this week, above the year-to-date average. The desk favors renting upside via limited-loss structures and pairing them with SPX lookback puts as its preferred hedge.
Megacap tech earnings and FOMC are the focus for the rest of the week. The implied move through Friday is 1.1%.
About two-thirds of SPX market cap will have reported earnings by Friday.
MSFT is up 50% from summer lows with an 8/10 GS positioning score. The implied earnings move is 4.7% versus a 15.5% move last quarter.
LLY is up 10.7% month to date with a 9/10 positioning score and a 6% implied move. It has traded higher on the last 4 consecutive prints.
MA is up 10.5% month to date with a 9/10 positioning score and a 2.7% implied move. Near-term put-call skew is flat, at the 6th percentile versus 5 years.

Cash and vol desks report investors starting to pick spots across AI. Mag 7 stocks are offered at cheap implied vol relative to the broader tech complex, with the ratio at the 15th percentile versus the last 4 years.
The neocloud basket (GSXUNEOC) is down over 28% month to date even after a 7% rally yesterday. The desk sees convertible bonds as an interesting way to play further reversion.

The NDX vs SPX implied vol spread blew out last week, then NDX vols underperformed meaningfully. The 1m ATM spread still ranks in the 94th percentile versus 4 years, but the 3-day compression was the largest seen in that period.

Interest in dispersion trades (short index vol, long single-stock vol) has risen. Rising NDX implied correlation has pushed the average single-stock-to-index vol ratio lower, which the desk calls an attractive entry point.

Light exotic structures are being offered as lower-cost alternatives to vanilla options, with discounts of up to ~66% to vanilla for comparable implementations. Knock-out calls on AI names are priced at 65-81% discounts to vanilla calls.

trade_ideas.description: SPX 31Mar27 90% lookback put with daily lookback until Dec 31, cost 1.82%
trade_ideas.rationale: Removes the need to time the top perfectly, for about 10bp premium to the average vanilla put price over the past 5 years. Allows for a possible Santa rally.

trade_ideas.description: 3m 105%/130% continuous knock-out calls on select AI names (AMAT 2.05%, AMD 1.85%, AVGO 2.46%, KLAC 1.84%, MU 2.03%)
trade_ideas.rationale: Capital-efficient way for investors expecting a cyclical 10% to 25% bounce rather than an unconstrained run, with 65-81% discounts to vanilla calls.
trade_ideas.risk: Knock-out if the stock touches or breaches the 130% barrier intraday.
